name: Trade-specific progress scopes
summary: Progress tracking for scopes the standard floor-plan flow does not fit: electrical work tracked against takeoff assets, building facades tracked on elevation drawings from drone captures, and underground utilities drawn on drone maps and kept in step with design drawings.

roles.note: The electrical PRD has support (TechOps) marking progress for clients; the facade PRD has field engineers creating facade zones. No dedicated permission strings exist. Zone strings from the seed catalog are listed where the PRD action is a zone action.

actions.action: Mark electrical progress against takeoff assets
Draw assets on a drone map

nfr.statement: Time for an asset drawn on a drone map to appear on the matching design drawing, and the reverse.
nfr.open_question: Must the two views agree as soon as the asset is saved, or may synchronisation run as a background step?

requirements.title: Electrical scopes are tracked at takeoff-asset level
requirements.statement: Takeoff assets for electrical scopes are ingested with their identifiers, codes, categories and stages. Support marks progress per capture against each takeoff asset, including partial counts, quantities or ratios, and can select and duplicate a takeoff asset together with its stages and measurements. The progress details panel shows each category's stages with progress aggregated from the takeoff assets, and identifiers are searchable.
requirements.rationale: PRD only as a whole. No duplicate-with-stages action or identifier search was traced. Client dashboards and automated detection are out of scope in the PRD.

sources.title: Prior PRDs - Takeoff management, electrical progress tracking and out-of-scope assets (t3d-prd-agent prd-organised)

acceptance_criteria.given: A set of electrical takeoff assets is ingested
acceptance_criteria.then: The assets are available with their identifiers, categories and stages

acceptance_criteria.given: Support marks 12 of 40 receptacles complete on a capture
acceptance_criteria.when: The progress details panel is opened
acceptance_criteria.then: The receptacle stage shows the aggregated progress from those takeoff assets

acceptance_criteria.given: The same takeoff asset is ingested twice
acceptance_criteria.then: No duplicate asset or corrupted data results

requirements.title: Facade progress is tracked on elevation drawings in facade zones
requirements.statement: Users create named polygonal zones tagged as facade zones on a structure and assign elevation drawings to them. Elevation drawings are flagged as facade drawings. Facade progress is a percentage complete, only drone captures can be assigned to it, and it is shown only on its elevation drawing. Facade and interior categories are kept apart: facade categories are not selectable on normal sheets and the reverse. Facade progress appears on the details, overview and trends pages, with N/A for structures that have none.
requirements.rationale: PRD only; no facade or elevation-drawing tracking was found in api-2d-progress or track3d-web. Whether facade and interior categories may be combined on trends or details, and zones versus sub-structures, are open (DEC-076).

A structure with no facade progress

requirements.title: Assets drawn on drone maps stay in step with design drawings
requirements.statement: Users draw polygons, lines and points on a drone map. Each asset is saved in site coordinates and appears on the matching design drawing, and assets drawn on a design appear on the drone map. Progress can be recorded against either. A design with no transformation cannot sync and the user is told; possible map inaccuracies are flagged.
requirements.rationale: PRD only. The code already converts design-drawn takeoff into site coordinates (PROG-REQ-055), but drawing on a drone map was not found (a drone-measurement out-of-scope switch exists only as commented-out code). AI extraction, auto-detection and terrain comparison are out of scope in the PRD.

requirements.title: Design-drawn takeoff is also stored in site coordinates
requirements.statement: Takeoff drawn on a design keeps its design coordinates and is converted to site coordinates through the design's transformation; if there is none, it is converted to BIM coordinates through the shortest available chain. Takeoff given in design coordinates must name a real design, or it is rejected.
